# Table of Contents

# 1\. Executive Summary

This document defines Module 09 - Settings & Configuration for iPOMS. It consolidates the complete business discussion - initial recommendations, business corrections, and final decisions - into a single functional specification.

Settings allows users and administrators to configure iPOMS according to their preferences without changing the application's business logic. It is the last of the core business modules before system-level planning begins.

# 2\. Purpose & Business Rule

Core business rule: Settings can customize the application; it cannot alter how placement operations work.

Examples of what belongs in Settings: changing the logo, changing a password, updating a profile picture, updating a mobile number.

Examples of what does not belong in Settings: changing how the Daily Tracker works, or changing report calculations - these remain governed by their respective business modules (Modules 2 and 6).

# 3\. Module Access

| **Role**              | **Access Level**                                            |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Placement Coordinator | Personal Settings only                                      |
| Team Leader           | Personal Settings + Limited System View                     |
| Director              | Personal Settings + Organization Settings + System Settings |
| CEO                   | Full Settings Access                                        |

# 4\. Module Structure

The Settings module contains five major sections, presented as a left-side navigation panel rather than horizontal tabs - chosen because it scales better as the application grows and matches the premium CRM style used throughout iPOMS:

- My Profile
- Security
- Application Settings
- Organization Settings (Director / CEO only)
- System Settings (Director / CEO only)

Privacy & Visibility is presented as a further read-only panel alongside these five. Everything stays inside one clean workspace with no pop-ups, no separate pages, and no nested menus.

# 5\. My Profile - Display Information

Every user can view their own profile. Displayed fields:

- Full Name
- Username
- Official Email ID
- Personal Email ID
- Official Mobile Number
- Personal Mobile Number
- Date of Birth
- Role
- Assigned Colleges
- Employee Status
- Current Residential Address

# 6\. My Profile - Editable vs Non-Editable Fields

Editable by the user:

- Personal Email
- Personal Mobile Number
- Alternate Mobile Number (optional, if included)
- Residential Address
- Profile Picture

Non-editable by the user - controlled only by Team Leader, Director, or CEO:

- Username
- Official Email
- Role
- Assigned Colleges

Only editable fields are rendered as input boxes on screen; every other field is displayed read-only.

# 7\. Security - Change Password

Available to every user. Flow: Current Password → New Password → Confirm Password → Save.

Password rules remain exactly as finalized in Module 08: minimum 8 characters, one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, one special character.

# 8\. Security - Active Sessions (Deferred)

An Active Sessions view (showing device, browser, and last login time, with an option to log out other devices) was discussed and removed from Version 1.0.

Reason: not currently required, and it adds unnecessary complexity for a small user base of around 20-25 users. It can be introduced later if multi-device session management becomes operationally important.

# 9\. Application Settings - Theme

Supported themes for Version 1.0: Light Theme, Dark Theme, High Contrast Theme, and System Default.

Although the product owner's personal preference is Light Mode, offering theme choice was retained for accessibility, and users may select whichever theme suits them without affecting business logic.

# 10\. Application Settings - Landing Page, Date & Time Format

Default Landing Page: users may choose where the application opens after login - Dashboard, Daily Tracker, or Weekly Tracker. This is a convenience setting and does not change business logic.

Date Format: fixed to the alphanumeric style, e.g. 24 July 2026, rather than a purely numeric format - judged easier to read.

Time Format: fixed to 12-hour format with AM/PM (e.g. 08:30 AM, 05:45 PM) for Version 1.0; 24-hour format is not offered.

# 11\. Application Settings - Notification Preferences

A separate notification module was previously removed from the product (see Module 07 discussion); Settings therefore provides only personal delivery preferences, not the notification content itself.

- Email Notifications - enabled/disabled
- System Notifications - enabled/disabled
- Dashboard Popup Notifications - enabled/disabled

These preferences are included in Version 1.0 even if email delivery is not fully implemented at launch, so the system remains extensible without a later redesign.

# 12\. Organization Settings (Director / CEO Only)

## 12.1 Organization Information

- Organization Name
- Organization Logo

## 12.2 Report Branding

Every exported report automatically displays the Organization Logo, Organization Name, Generated By, Generated Date, and Footer Text - configured once here rather than hardcoded into report templates (directly supports Module 06 - Reports & Analytics).

## 12.3 Support Information

- Support Email
- Support Mobile Number
- Office Address (optional)

Useful if the application grows to serve more than a single office.

# 13\. System Settings (Director / CEO Only)

## 13.1 Application Information (Display Only)

- Application Version
- Build Version
- Last Updated Date

## 13.2 Database Summary (Read-Only)

- Total Users
- Total Coordinators
- Total Companies
- Total HR Contacts
- Total Colleges

This information is read-only and informational - Settings never exposes an editing interface over these figures.

# 14\. Backup & Restore - Decision

Question raised: should Version 1.0 give users a Backup/Restore control?

Decision: no. Whichever backend is ultimately chosen (Firebase or MongoDB Atlas), backups should be handled by the administrator or cloud infrastructure, not exposed through the application UI.

Instead, Version 1.0 displays only a simple reassurance panel: Database Status - Connected, Last Synchronization - Today. If manual exports are wanted in future, Export Users (Excel), Export Metadata (Excel), and Export Reports (PDF/Excel) are more operationally useful than a manual database backup control, and can be added later.

# 15\. Profile Picture

Users can upload, change, or remove their profile picture. It is displayed in the Dashboard, User Profile, and User List - making the application feel more personal and easier to navigate.

# 16\. Privacy & Visibility Settings

Rather than hiding visibility rules only in code, iPOMS shows them to users as informational read-only settings. The frozen business rule:

- Official Email - visible based on work requirements.
- Personal Email - visible only to Team Leader, Director, and CEO.
- Official Mobile - visible where needed for work.
- Personal Mobile Number - visible only to Team Leader, Director, and CEO.
- Residential Address - visible only to Team Leader, Director, and CEO.
- Other Coordinators - cannot view another coordinator's personal information.

This protects personal data while still allowing management to contact employees when necessary. Since these are organizational policies rather than personal preferences, coordinators see them as read-only; only administrators can change the underlying policy.

# 17\. System Announcement Banner

Approved for Version 1.0. Distinct from personal notifications - it communicates organization-wide information such as scheduled maintenance, a new placement policy, a holiday announcement, an urgent team meeting, or a system update.

Only the Director or CEO can create or remove an announcement. Every logged-in user sees the active announcement until it expires or is removed. The publishing interface itself (title, message, start date, end date, publish) lives operationally in Module 10 - System Information & Administration, which owns announcement management day to day.

# 18\. UI Design Direction

Settings is presented as a single-workspace admin panel, not a long scrolling page: a left-side navigation panel lists My Profile, Security, Application, Organization, System, and Privacy; selecting an item loads that section into a large content area with a single Save action at the bottom.

Only editable fields render as input controls; every other field is shown read-only, consistent with the rule in Section 6. This layout was chosen over horizontal tabs because it scales more gracefully as further settings are added in future versions.

# 19\. Features Excluded from Version 1.0

- Multi-language / locale selection
- API configuration
- Email server configuration
- Technical developer settings
- Advanced dashboard customization
- Active Session Management (see Section 8)
- Manual Backup/Restore interface (see Section 14)

These can be introduced in future versions if business needs evolve; excluding them keeps Version 1.0 focused on what the team will actually use.

# 20\. Business Rules Summary

- Settings customizes the application; it never changes business workflow or report calculation logic.
- Only Personal Email, Personal Mobile, Alternate Mobile, Residential Address, and Profile Picture are user-editable; Username, Official Email, Role, and Assigned Colleges are organization-controlled.
- Password rules are inherited unchanged from Module 08 - no duplicate policy is defined here.
- Date format is fixed to an alphanumeric style (24 July 2026); time format is fixed to 12-hour AM/PM for Version 1.0.
- Report branding (logo, organization name, generated-by, generated-date, footer) is configured once in Organization Settings and applied automatically to every exported report.
- Backups remain an infrastructure responsibility, not a user-facing control, in Version 1.0.
- Personal Mobile, Personal Email, and Residential Address are visible only to Team Leader, Director, and CEO - never to other coordinators.
- Only the Director or CEO may publish or remove a System Announcement Banner; every logged-in user sees it until expiry.

# 21\. Deferred / Out of Scope for v1.0

- Active Session Management (multi-device logout).
- Manual Backup/Restore controls in the UI.
- Multi-language support, API configuration, and email server configuration.
- Advanced/custom dashboard layout settings.
- Alternate Mobile Number field (included only if the business decides it is needed).

# 22\. Conclusion

Module 09 is considered functionally complete for Version 1.0. Settings & Configuration now gives every user control over their personal profile, security, and preferences, gives Director/CEO organization-wide branding and system controls, and gives every user visibility into the privacy rules that protect their personal data - without ever touching the business workflows defined in Modules 1-8.

# 23\. Next Module

Module 10 - System Information & Administration: the compact management dashboard that gives the Director and CEO a single view of system health, organization snapshot, database growth, and data quality, and that operationally owns creation of the announcements introduced in this module.
